narration: Every building has a life story. And its carbon is written into every chapter.
Chapter one: materials. Rock is quarried, crushed and baked. Cement and steel alone produce around fifteen percent of the world's CO2.
Chapter two: construction. Trucks, cranes and waste. By opening day, all of that carbon is already in the air.
Chapter three: life. Decades of cooling, heating and lighting. Plus every repair and replacement along the way.
Chapter four: the end. Demolition and landfill. Or, a second life through reuse.
Many green claims read only chapter three. A life cycle assessment reads the whole book.
And it matters. Between now and 2050, about half the carbon from new construction is expected to be released before anyone moves in.
So when you hear the words green building, ask one thing. Which chapters did they count?
